evidence.why: Four-pointer type and four separate file-local declarations.
Initializer uses array-style destinations for the four resource families.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported record structure and resource mapping while removing unsupported compiled-layout certainty.
facts.value: Source-level asset storage consists of four separately declared static MnVibrationJointAssets objects. Each record declares joint, animjoint, matanim and shapeanim pointers. Initialization indexes from &mnVibration_804A0868 as though these records form an array: entry 0 supplies the cursor joint, entry 1 controller-panel resources, entry 2 saved-name ON/OFF resources, and entry 3 main-screen resources. This establishes the source access assumption, not the compiled section's exact size or contiguity.

evidence.why: Consumes resource names through the layout cast.

facts.rationale: The layout cast is supported, but the previous 504-byte contiguous compiled-block claim requires compiled evidence.
facts.value: The source defines a MnVibrationDataLayout interpretation containing three AnimLoopSettings records, one Vec3, diagnostic strings and archive-resource names. Corresponding objects are declared separately beginning with mnVibration_803EECE0, whose address is cast to this layout by consumers. The supported interpretation is presentation configuration accessed through that layout; exact compiled section extent and contiguity are not established by these declarations.

evidence.why: Cancel precedes the independent byte-counter gate.
Indicator descriptor endpoints select panel presentation.

facts.rationale: Corrects the conflation of animation progress with input gating and preserves the early-cancel exception and uncertain third descriptor field.
facts.value: Declares animation-setting triples {0,20,-0.1}, {50,70,-0.1} and {0,14,-0.1}. Intro presentation changes to the steady process when its helper-reported frame reaches 20; exit presentation requests destruction when its helper-reported frame reaches 70. The indicator descriptor supplies endpoints 0 and 14 to panel presentation. Ordinary input is separately gated by byte counter x0[0] against intro end_frame, after cooldown and cancel handling. The third initializer value is preserved without identifying it as a frame step absent the animation-helper contract.

evidence.why: Combines saved-name text and rumble-state animation.
Settings Rumble selection invokes the screen initializer.

facts.rationale: Preserves the row's user-facing meaning while replacing unsupported literal Records-menu placement with the demonstrated entry path.
facts.value: Renders one saved-player-name entry in Melee's rumble-settings interface, pairing the name text with an animated display of that name's persistent rumble preference. The containing screen is entered through the Settings menu's Rumble selection.

evidence.why: Complete input handler establishes branch order, early returns, numeric tests and navigation.

facts.rationale: Makes the actual priority, independent counter, absence of a local connectivity gate and numeric selection-mode semantics explicit.
facts.value: Shared cooldown returns first. Once it expires, cancel takes priority over the intro gate and performs transition, text cleanup, main-screen destruction request, rumble removal and a power-time update. Otherwise x0[0] is incremented and the callback returns while that byte counter is at most intro end_frame. Port confirmations are then checked in order 0 through 3 for selection mode x0[port+2] == 0, without an explicit connectivity check; the first qualifying confirmation toggles the persistent port preference and returns after stopping rumble or starting a preview. With names present, left/right switches per-controller selection mode between 0 and 1, and masks from mode-1 controllers are combined for the name list. Name confirmation has priority, maps a flag equal to 1 to false and any other value to true, and animates the selected row. Otherwise up takes priority over down, moving to a valid adjacent visible row or changing the scroll offset and rebuilding rows at a boundary. These mode bytes are neither persistent rumble values nor connection flags.

evidence.why: Ordered cooldown, cancel, counter, port and name-mode behavior.
Exit completion and recurring connection transitions.

facts.rationale: Replaces blanket animation-time input blocking and implied connectivity gating with the actual input and lifecycle state transitions.
facts.value: The input callback returns during shared cooldown, then permits cancel before applying its separate introductory byte-counter gate to ordinary actions. After that gate, selection mode 0 permits per-port confirmation, while mode 1 contributes input to the shared saved-name list; the handler does not explicitly gate these paths on connectivity. Port confirmation disables rumble with removal/off operations or enables it with a preview. Separately, the recurring presentation process updates all four rumble displays and reconciles live PAD errors with cached connection bytes: disconnect hides and refreshes the control, while reconnect also resets selection mode to 0. Leaving menu 19 switches a surviving main-screen process to exit-animation completion; cancellation has its own direct cleanup path, and the independent cursor has its own menu-lifetime callback.
